claim: Parameter-based knowledge editing cannot reliably update factual knowledge in a large language model without damaging its core capabilities. The near-perfect editing results reported in prior work do not survive realistic evaluation, and the limitation is geometric rather than incidental: localized weight edits are disproportionately amplified along low-variance directions of the model's representation space and propagate globally, so damage compounds as edits accumulate. A parameter-free approach that leaves the weights untouched is therefore a serious alternative to parameter editing rather than a fallback.
experiments_evaluated: To address subclaims 1, 2, 5, and 6, reproduce representative parameter-editing methods such as ROME, MEMIT, and a fine-tuning baseline on at least two publicly available model families, for example GPT-J-6B and Pythia-6.9B. Apply 1, 10, 100, and 1,000 sequential edits drawn from the public CounterFact, zsRE, and MQuAKE datasets, using multiple random edit orders and seeds. First report the methods' original benchmark metrics; then evaluate held-out paraphrases, aliases, multi-hop questions, contradictory-context prompts, and delayed re-evaluation. Measure global effects on unrelated facts, WikiText-103 perplexity, and public core-capability benchmarks including MMLU, ARC-Challenge, HellaSwag, and WinoGrande. Include unedited-model, norm-matched random-update, and ordinary fine-tuning controls, and preregister reliability as simultaneously maintaining edit success, paraphrase generalization, specificity, and core-capability scores within a narrow confidence bound of the unedited model. Plot every metric against edit count and test whether damage grows linearly or superlinearly while controlling for edit difficulty and order. If original metrics remain near-perfect but realistic tests or unrelated capabilities deteriorate, this supports the claim that prior results do not survive realistic evaluation, that effects propagate globally, and that damage compounds. Stable generalization and capabilities through many edits would refute or sharply qualify those subclaims. This experiment could be reduced or omitted if prior work releases complete sequential checkpoints, edit orders, and outputs on the same independent capability suite, permitting an equivalent audit.

To address subclaims 3 and 4, test the proposed geometric mechanism causally rather than relying only on correlations. For each model and edited layer from Experiment 1, estimate the hidden-state covariance eigenspectrum using a fixed public corpus such as WikiText-103 or The Pile validation data. Decompose each learned weight update and its induced activation change into low-, middle-, and high-variance covariance eigenspaces. Measure amplification as output or logit change per unit update norm, and relate low-variance alignment to edit success, unrelated-prompt drift, perplexity change, and benchmark damage. Then construct norm- and rank-matched interventions that place otherwise comparable updates predominantly in low-variance versus high-variance subspaces; also project actual editor updates away from low-variance directions and, where necessary, retune their magnitude to match edit success. Use bootstrap confidence intervals across layers, facts, models, and seeds. Disproportionately large and widespread behavioral changes from low-variance-aligned updates, plus reduced collateral damage after removing those components at matched edit success, would provide causal evidence for the geometric account. No amplification difference, failure to replicate across models, or damage explained by update norm, layer, or optimization instability would favor an incidental rather than geometric explanation. Existing evidence would make this experiment unnecessary only if it included released activations and checkpoints plus norm-matched, edit-success-matched causal subspace interventions across multiple models.

To address subclaims 7 and 8, compare the strongest parameter editor from Experiment 1 with a parameter-free external-memory system under matched factual updates and operational budgets. Store CounterFact, zsRE, and MQuAKE updates in a versioned text index, retrieve relevant records, and insert them into a fixed prompt without changing model parameters; include retrieval-only, oracle-retrieval, no-retrieval, and irrelevant-retrieval controls. Verify the parameter-free property by hashing every model tensor before and after all updates, checking that no optimizer state or adapter is attached, and separately reporting changes to the external index and prompt. Evaluate single and sequential updates using the same efficacy, paraphrase, multi-hop, specificity, global-capability, and accumulation tests as Experiment 1, while also measuring retrieval failures, answer conflicts, context-window pressure, latency, storage, update and deletion cost, and performance when the relevant record is not retrieved. Predefine serious alternative as noninferior realistic edit accuracy and materially lower collateral damage at an acceptable, explicitly reported resource cost, rather than requiring superiority on every dimension. If external memory preserves core capabilities and matches or exceeds parameter editing under these constraints, it is a credible alternative; if it works only with oracle retrieval, excessive context, or direct answer leakage and fails on natural variants, it is better characterized as a fallback. Identical tensor hashes establish that the model weights remain untouched, although they do not establish that the overall system is unchanged. A trusted reproducible artifact with immutable weight hashes could remove the need for the weight-integrity check, but not for the comparative evaluation.
reference_experiments: Fix the measurement floor and the inference protocol before editing anything. Score the unedited model on the editing benchmark to establish the pre-edit baseline, and re-run single-edit evaluation of existing methods under plain autoregressive decoding rather than the teacher-forced protocol prior work used, since teacher forcing supplies the ground-truth answer tokens at inference and inflates every number. If methods keep their near-perfect single-edit scores under honest decoding there is no discrepancy to explain. The authors report a pre-edit baseline of Reliability 3.00, Generalization 3.00, Locality 15.50, Portability 4.36 on ZsRE, and a best parameter-based single-edit average of 25.99.

Validate the scoring instrument before quoting any number from it. Judge semantic consistency of generated answers with a strong LLM across reliability, generalization, locality and portability, then cross-check that ranking with a deterministic token-level measure (match ratio and exact match) that does not depend on a model's opinion. If the two disagree, every result is an artifact of the judge rather than a property of the editing methods. The authors find the token-level check reproduces the semantic ranking, with the pre-edit model at 100% by definition and GRACE holding 100% under both single and sequential editing.

Test the asserted mechanism directly. Take the SVD of the original hidden-representation matrix, compute the directional relative change rate R_k = sqrt(n)|u_k^T delta_h| / sigma_k for each principal direction after an edit, and check where amplification concentrates and how it behaves as edits accumulate. The claim's causal story requires R_k > 1 predominantly in low-singular-value directions with the fraction rising monotonically with edit count, across methods and architectures.

Run the main benchmark. Compare eleven editing methods spanning locate-then-edit (ROME, MEMIT, PMET, RECT, AlphaEdit, FT-L), meta-learning (MEND), additional-parameter (AdaLoRA, WISE) and external-memory (GRACE, SCR) families, under sequential editing at 1, 10, 100 and full-dataset edit counts, on ZsRE and WikiData-counterfact, across Llama-2-7B-Chat, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Mistral-7B-Instruct and DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B, reporting all four dimensions. The claim holds if every parameter-modifying method degrades toward zero as edits accumulate and the parameter-free retrieval baseline outscores all of them; the authors report ROME, RECT, FT-L, MEND and AdaLoRA at 0.00-0.25 average under sequential editing on DeepSeek-R1-Distill, against SCR at 56.59 single and 60.19 sequential.

Measure damage to capabilities the edits never targeted. Take the models edited in the main benchmark and evaluate them on mathematical reasoning (AIME 2024, AIME 2025, AMC, OlympiadBench, MATH-500) and broad benchmarks (GPQA-Diamond, ARC-c, MMLU-Pro), reporting accuracy after 10 and after 100 sequential edits. Without this the study would only show editing is ineffective, not that it is damaging. The authors report ROME and RECT losing 2.74 and 8.37 average accuracy at 10 edits and falling to near zero at 100, with MEND at 0.00 after both.

Rule out that the result is an artifact of scale, knowledge type, fact difficulty or one method's configuration. Repeat the sweep on larger models (Llama-2-13B, Qwen3-14B), on event-level knowledge (ELKEN, with events converted to triples for the parameter-based arms), split by high- and low-confidence fact sets, and probe the hyperparameter and architecture sensitivity of AlphaEdit — the one method that does not collapse — including its failure to run on Llama-2 and Mistral. If the collapse disappears at 13-14B or only occurs on triple-shaped facts, the claim is bounded rather than general.

reference_coverage.adequacy: A clean pre-edit performance floor and a single-edit comparison under ordinary unconstrained generation, allowing inflation from an inference protocol to be separated from genuine editing success.
reference_coverage.rationale: Proposed experiment 0 includes unedited-model controls, a one-edit condition, reproduction of the original benchmark results, and a subsequent realistic generation-based evaluation. This would let the team compare the apparent near-perfect result with performance under realistic evaluation and establish the pre-edit floor.

reference_coverage.adequacy: An independent semantic assessment and deterministic token-level check whose agreement can distinguish a real editing-method ranking from an artifact of the scoring model.
reference_coverage.rationale: The proposed experiments specify efficacy, generalization, specificity, capability, and retrieval metrics, but do not require an independent semantic-versus-deterministic token-level cross-check of the editing scores.
reasoning_chain: The reference experiment establishes whether conclusions about editing quality and method ranking are robust to the choice of scoring instrument.
The proposed set reports many outcomes but never requires agreement between a semantic judge and a deterministic token-level measure, nor any comparable scorer-validation procedure.
Therefore a favorable or unfavorable ranking could still be caused by the chosen evaluator rather than by the editing behavior.
A team running the proposed set would fail to learn whether the reported editing results are robust to scoring-instrument artifacts.

reference_coverage.adequacy: A normalized, direction-resolved measurement of representation change relative to variance, tracked over cumulative edit counts and replicated across layers, methods, and architectures, together with a way to distinguish geometric amplification from update-size confounds.
reference_coverage.rationale: Experiment 0 supplies multiple cumulative edit counts and several editors and model families. Experiment 1 estimates the representation covariance eigenspectrum, decomposes induced activation changes by variance subspace, measures amplification per unit update norm, and adds norm- and rank-matched low- versus high-variance interventions with edit-success matching. This directly tests low-variance amplification and its accumulation while addressing update-norm, layer, and optimization alternatives.

reference_coverage.adequacy: Evidence that the observed limitation is not tied to one editor, architecture, or factual benchmark, obtained by comparing multiple parameter-editing approaches across diverse settings and cumulative edit loads.
reference_coverage.rationale: Proposed experiment 0 compares multiple parameter-editing approaches across two model families, three factual-update datasets, several edit counts, random orders and seeds, and multiple reliability/generalization/locality-style outcomes. Experiment 2 adds a direct comparison with an external-memory alternative under matched updates and budgets. This provides the requisite cross-method, cross-model, cross-data, and sequential evidence without needing the reference's exact method roster.

reference_coverage.adequacy: An independent assessment of untargeted core capabilities at early and larger cumulative edit counts, with an unedited comparison, so capability damage can be distinguished from failure to perform the requested edits.
reference_coverage.rationale: Proposed experiment 0 evaluates unrelated facts, perplexity, and several independent core-capability benchmarks at 1, 10, 100, and 1,000 edits, alongside an unedited-model control. In particular, it includes the 10- and 100-edit checkpoints needed to detect collateral degradation rather than merely poor edit reliability.

reference_coverage.adequacy: Stress tests that separate model scale, knowledge representation and type, fact difficulty, and editor configuration as explanations for the observed collapse, including larger systems and focused sensitivity analysis.
reference_coverage.rationale: The proposed set does test multiple model families and factual datasets, uses difficulty and edit-order controls, and varies layers, seeds, update norms, ranks, and subspaces. However, it does not require a larger-scale model sweep, an event-level knowledge condition distinct from triple-shaped facts, confidence-stratified facts, or a focused hyperparameter/architecture sensitivity and failure analysis of a method that appears robust.
reasoning_chain: The reference experiment tests whether the conclusion changes with model scale, knowledge representation, fact confidence, and editor configuration.
The proposed set varies model family, dataset, edit difficulty/order, layers, seeds, and intervention geometry, so it addresses some but not all of those possible explanations.
It leaves larger-scale models, event-level knowledge, confidence strata, and targeted editor hyperparameter/architecture sensitivity unresolved.
Thus any observed collapse or stability remains compatible with an untested scale, knowledge-type, or configuration confound.
A team running the proposed set would fail to learn how far the conclusion generalizes beyond its tested model, fact, and editor settings.

sufficiency_reasoning: The proposed set directly tests realistic sequential editing and collateral capability damage, probes the geometric mechanism with causal subspace interventions, and verifies and benchmarks a parameter-free external-memory alternative. Those experiments would substantially settle the substantive claim. It would not fully settle the claim as robustly as the reference set because the scoring instrument is not independently validated against a deterministic token-level measure, and the robustness sweep omits larger scale, event-level knowledge, confidence strata, and focused editor-configuration sensitivity.
missing: Add a scorer-validation experiment comparing semantic judgments with deterministic token-level match and exact-match measures across all four editing dimensions.
Extend the robustness sweep to larger models, event-level facts, confidence-stratified fact sets, and systematic hyperparameter and architecture sensitivity of any editor that does not collapse.
